priorFindingsResolution.priorSummary: python-runner.integration.test.ts broken (1 pass, 2 fail), required CI lane producer
priorFindingsResolution.evidence: Independently reran the file standalone: 4 pass / 0 fail / 50 expect() calls (was 1 pass / 2 fail / 5 expect() calls). Test rewritten to call c02_runner.py without the removed --sdk-bridge/--node flags, now asserts issue-code equality (not just ok/not-ok) between the Bun and host-Python runtimes, and adds a new 'malformed envelope' negative case. The file is now included in the 19-file focused-suite bundle used for coverage (it was silently absent from the 18-file bundle at the prior head, which is part of why the break went unnoticed). scripts/check-factory-lanes.ts still declares it as a producer of the 'Factory runner contracts' lane (scripts/check-factory-lanes.ts:72, .github/workflows/ci.yml:117) and check-factory-lanes.ts reruns green (exit 0).

priorFindingsResolution.priorSummary: TRUST_TRANSITIONS.publish.from included 'revoked', letting a plain publish reactivate a revoked package
priorFindingsResolution.evidence: TRUST_TRANSITIONS.publish.from is now ['none','active','quarantined'] (revoked removed); quarantine.from is ['active']; revoke.from is ['active','quarantined']. Once state is 'revoked', no entry in any transition's 'from' array includes 'revoked', so publish/quarantine/revoke all throw factory_package_trust_conflict from that state -- verified by reading src/factory/package-preparation.ts:76-140 directly. Grepped the whole src tree for every writer of factory_runner_package_trust_current/factory_runner_package_trust_revisions: only package-preparation.ts's change() method writes them at runtime (migrations only touch them at migrate-time). New tests 'revocation is terminal for its pinned tuple and no transition leaves it' and the rewritten 'prepares an exact active v4 release...' test (both in src/__tests__/helpers/factory-package-preparation-suite.ts, run via src/factory/package-preparation.integration.test.ts on PGlite and tests/postgres/factory-package-preparation.test.ts on real PostgreSQL) assert publish/quarantine/revoke from 'revoked' all reject with factory_package_trust_conflict, and that a replacement requires a new pinned reference (new digest) starting its own trust chain from 'none'. Independently reran; both pass as part of the 175/0/786 focused-suite result below.

priorFindingsResolution.priorSummary: scripts/coverage-thresholds.json (W18-owned) edited without being listed among landed deviations
priorFindingsResolution.status: resolved, with a new minor side-effect
priorFindingsResolution.evidence: New deviation 9 in tasks/factory/w02-GATES.md explicitly names the coverage-thresholds.json edit and its justification (common.md requires a 100% key per new file). However the delta's actual diff to that file does not add any new key (the two new keys were already present at the prior head); it only changes the indentation of two pre-existing, unrelated keys (packages/@ezcorp/factory-sdk/src/parse.ts and .../page-bytes.ts) from 2-space to 4-space, reintroducing an inconsistency the original W02 branch had already cleaned up. This contradicts deviation 9's own claim that the edit is 'appended textually so no other line in the file moves.' Confirmed cosmetic only: bun run lint (biome check) and bunx biome check scripts/coverage-thresholds.json both exit 0, and the file still parses and gates correctly (new-file/patch coverage gates both pass). See new finding L4 below.

priorFindingsResolution.priorSummary: No Promise.all concurrent race test for the device-exclusivity fence
priorFindingsResolution.evidence: New test 'two simultaneous claims for the same device on one host settle with exactly one winner' in tests/postgres/factory-executions.test.ts uses a real 4-connection PostgreSQL pool and Promise.all(attempts.map(...claimStart...)) so the two transactions genuinely overlap. Independently reran under the heavy lock against real PostgreSQL: 9 pass / 0 fail / 2667 expect() calls across factory-executions.test.ts + factory-schema.test.ts (was previously a narrower subset). This test is also the one that surfaced the real JSONB storage defect (see below): PGlite hid the bug because it hands back parsed objects, while Bun's SQL driver types a string parameter as json, making the old `${text}::jsonb` cast a no-op that stored a JSON string scalar.

priorFindingsResolution.priorSummary: No concurrent-quarantine-vs-in-flight-attempt test and no crash-mid-fence fault injection for quarantine()/revoke()
priorFindingsResolution.evidence: New test 'a stop path that crashes mid-fence leaves the package active rather than half-quarantined' adds a controlled fault (a fenceAttempts double that can be told to throw) and proves the trust-state write and the fence call commit or fail together (state stays '1:active' after the crash; a retry with the fence healthy commits both). This is a genuine, real fault-injection test and directly closes the 'crash-mid-fence' half of L2, reran independently as part of the 175/0/786 focused-suite result. The other half of L2 -- a true Promise.all race between an in-flight dispatch/attempt and a concurrent quarantine()/revoke() call -- was not added; every quarantine/revoke case remains sequential. Remains LOW severity and non-blocking, same as originally scored.

newFindings.summary: The coverage-thresholds.json edit in this delta reformats two pre-existing, unrelated keys' indentation (2-space to 4-space) rather than being a pure append, contradicting deviation 9's claim that 'no other line in the file moves.' Purely cosmetic (JSON is whitespace-insensitive; bun run lint / bunx biome check both exit 0 on the file; coverage gates still pass), but it silently reverts a cleanup the original W02 branch had already made to that file.

This delta's JSONB fix touches src/factory/runner/attempt-runtime.ts and adds a new test file section to tests/postgres/factory-executions.test.ts. Per freeze section 12's ownership table (interfaces doc line 2088), attempt-runtime.ts's default owner is Terra runtime (W01); the doc's frozen-type section only carves out a narrower joint W01/W02 write for the FactoryAttemptDeviceGrant/FactoryAttemptLaunchIntent interfaces specifically. The jsonColumn() fix goes beyond that carve-out: it also changes how request_json, package_receipt_json, and terminal_result_json are decoded (not just device_grant_json), which is W01's general attempt-launch persistence, not W02's device-authority surface. The change is technically sound, thoroughly tested, and extensively narrated inside gate G2a (which explains the defect and fix in detail) -- but unlike every other cross-ownership touch in this branch (schema.ts/migrate.ts as deviation 6, coverage-thresholds.json as deviation 9), it is not listed in the 'Landed deviations for the coordinator' section, which is the disclosure mechanism this same gate file otherwise uses consistently. This is the same class of gap as the previously-fixed M3, recurring on a new, more consequential file. Recommend adding an 11th landed deviation pointing at G2a.
